Bug_Details:
Reports comparisons with double and float `NaN` (Not-a-Number) values.
            These are [specified](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.21.1)
            to have unintuitive behavior: NaN is considered unequal to itself.
            This means a check like `someDouble == Double.NaN` will always return
            false, even if `someDouble` is really the NaN value. To test whether a
            value is the NaN value, one should instead use `Double.isNaN(someDouble)`
            (or `Float.isNaN`). The `!=` operator should be treated similarly.
            Finally, comparisons like `someDouble <= Double.NaN` are nonsensical
            and will always evaluate to false.
            
            This rule has been renamed from "BadComparison" in PMD 6.36.0.
Examples:
boolean x = (y == Double.NaN);
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the `showBug` method where a double value is compared with NaN using the `==` operator. According to the Java specification, this comparison will always return false, even if the double value is actually NaN.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case passed a NaN value to the `showBug` method, which compared the value with NaN using the `==` operator. According to Java's specification, this comparison will always return false, even if the double value is NaN. To trigger the bug, the JUnit test makes an assertFalse call, expecting the method to return false, which will fail the test.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the bug was triggered. The test case 'testShowBugWithNaN' passed, which means that the method'showBug' returned false when it was given the value Double.NaN. However, according to the bug description, this should not be the case. The comparison 'value == Double.NaN' should always return true if 'value' is Double.NaN, but the test result shows that it returned false. This confirms that the bug is present in the code.
